newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Copper, aluminium watching strikes.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Copper, aluminium watching strikes.

text.p: 3 MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
---------------VIEWS FROM THE MARKET - April 22 ---------------
Copper prices could test resistance at $2,300 and higher as the technical picture shows signs of improving, analysts said. The strike at Chile's Escondida mine is helping to underpin the market.
Aluminium's charts are mixed but a 24-hour strike at Australia's Alcoa mines and refineries may tip the scales higher.
COPPER - Analysts and traders gave copper a decent chance of breaking higher, with a squeeze in nearby dates and an ongoing strike in Chile's Escondida copper mine helping fend off downside attacks.
On the upside $2,300 and then $2,320 were targets if prices managed to break out of the $2,245-$2,297 range which has trapped prices in recent days.
Late on Monday Escondida's CEO said the strike, which started on Friday, had slowed down operations slightly, although output of concentrates and cathodes was normal.
Traders said the strike, held by 350 of the mine's 2,000 employees was helping to underpin the market but had yet to make a significant impact on prices.
"If the market was really worried we'd be at $2,350 right now. This strike is not going to last long and it's a minority of workers," a trader said.
Copper was also benefiting from tightness in April and May dates, which pushed cash to threes backwardation out to $68/$71 on Tuesday morning, compared to around $30 at the end of last week.
Chartwise, the 10-day moving average looked to have made a bottom and was turning higher from the current $2,280 level.
At 0745 GMT three months copper was indicated at $2,295 per tonne, versus Monday's late close of $2,287/91.

ALUMINIUM - Prices ticked higher on Tuesday morning, helped by firmer copper and news of a 24-hour strike at the Western Australia operations of aluminium and bauxite producer Alcoa of Australia Ltd, traders said.
Mine officials said the strike would not stop production.
"Still, it might give the market a little impetus," a trader said, noting that aluminium has been moving sideways in a $1,540-$1,560 since April 14.
Higher up aluminium would encounter pockets of resistance at $1,575 and then $1,590, although the psychological $1,600 level would be a more difficult barrier to hurdle, analysts said.
Aluminium's downside was limited due to a wide chasm between the 10- and 30-day moving averages and very low near-term stochasYics, analysts said.
At 0745 GMT three months aluminium was quoted at $1,565 per tonne, compared to Monday's late close of $1,554/57.
--Lida Poletz, London newsroom +44 171 542 2936
